title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option B1: Anglo-Saxon and Norman England, c1060–88

exam_structure.overview: Tests British depth across 3 Key Topics. Q1(a)/(b) Describe features (4m), Q2 Explain why causation (12m), Q3/Q4 Choice essay with stimulus points (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: Anglo-Saxon England and the Norman Conquest, 1060–66

topics.title: 1. Anglo-Saxon government, economy and society
points: Monarchy & government; power of the English monarchy; Earldoms, local government & the legal system
Economy & social system; Towns & villages; influence of the Church

topics.title: 2. The last years of Edward the Confessor and the succession crisis
points: Power & significance of house of Godwin; Harold Godwinson’s succession as Earl of Wessex
Harold Godwinson’s embassy to Normandy; reasons for the rising against Tostig & his exile; death of Edward the Confessor

topics.title: 3. The rival claimants for the throne
points: Motives & claims of William of Normandy, Harald Hardrada & Edgar the Aethling
The Witan & the coronation & reign of Harold Godwinson
Causes & significance: outcome of the battles of Gate Fulford & Stamford Bridge

topics.title: 4. The Norman invasion
points: The Battle of Hastings
Causes of William’s victory (incl. the leadership skills of Harold & William, Norman & English troops & tactics)

sections.title: Key topic 2: William I in power: securing the kingdom, 1066–87

topics.title: 1. Establishing control
points: Submission of the earls, 1066
Rewarding followers & establishing control on the borderlands through the use of earls; The Marcher earldoms
Causes of building of castles; their key features & importance

topics.title: 2. Anglo-Saxon resistance, 1068–71
points: Causes & outcomes of Anglo-Saxon resistance: the revolt of Earls Edwin & Morcar (1068); Edgar the Aethling & the rebellions in the North (1069); Hereward the Wake & rebellion at Ely (1070–71 )

topics.title: 3. The legacy of resistance to 1087
points: Reasons for & features of Harrying of the North (1069–70); Its immediate & long-term impact, 1069–87
Changes in landownership from Anglo-Saxon to Norman, 1066–87

topics.title: 4. Revolt of the Earls, 1075
points: Causes of & features of the revolt
Defeat of the revolt & its effects

topics.title: 1. The feudal system and the Church
points: Feudal hierarchy; role & importance of tenants-in-chief & knights; nature of feudalism (landholding, homage, knight service, labour service); forfeiture
The Church in England: its role in society & relationship to government (incl. Stigand & Lanfranc); The Normanisation & reform of the Church in the reign of William I
Scale of change to Anglo-Saxon society & economy

topics.title: 2. Norman government
points: Changes to government after the Conquest; Centralised power & the limited use of earls under William I; regents during William’s absences
Office of sheriff & the demesne; Introduction & significance of the ‘forest’
The Domesday survey & Domesday Book & their significance for Norman government & finance

topics.title: 3. The Norman aristocracy
points: Culture & language of the Norman aristocracy
Career & significance of Bishop Odo

topics.title: 4. William I and the succession
points: Character & personality of William I & his relations with Robert (incl. Robert’s revolt in Normandy (1077–80)
William’s death & the disputed succession; William Rufus & the defeat of Robert & Odo
